AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
The invitation code from the invitation link, and the names of a person the catalog does not know yet, each within the API's limit.
The API trims each name before it counts its length. A user the catalog knows sends none.

AuditActorResponse.description:
Who acted: a user, by catalog user id, or the platform, that is a system admin seen from a tenant's log. `displayName` is a
user's real name, or null: for a user without a name, a deleted user, a user the catalog does not know, and for the platform, which
the screen names from `kind` in its own language. `deleted` is set for a user only.

AuditActorResponseKind.description: The kind of actor of an audit record.

AuditEntryResponse.description:
One record of an audit log: when, the operation (`member.invited`), who acted, what it was done to, and the details the record
keeps (a JSON object, or null). Names are resolved when the log is read; a name is only a person's real name. It holds no email
address.

AuditOperation.description: The operation of an audit record, area.action.

AuditTargetResponse.description:
What the action was done to: a tenant with its name at that moment, a user with their real name now or null, or an invitation, which
has no name. `deleted` is set for a user only.

AuditTargetResponseKind.description: The kind of target of an audit record.

ChangeMemberRoleRequest.description:
The built-in role to give the member. The role is required: a request without one is refused, so it never falls back to the enum's
first value.

ChangePreferencesRequest.description:
The user's language, one of the list, and the IANA name of their time zone, such as `Europe/Dublin`, or null for "not set":
the web then uses the browser's. Both are required, so a client that leaves the time zone out never clears it by mistake.

CreateTenantRequest.description:
A new tenant, the email address of its first owner, who is invited once the tenant is ready, and the language of the owner's
invitation email: without one, the system admin's own. The API trims the name before it counts its length.

ErrorCode.description: The error's code, area.reason. A client shows its own text for it, never the English detail.

FieldErrorCode.description: Why one field of a request failed validation.

GetInvitationPreviewRequest.description: The invitation code from the invitation link.

InvitationPreviewResponse.description:
What the accept screen shows the invited person before they accept: the tenant's name, who invited, the role the invitation
gives, when it expires, and its state at the moment of the request: `pending`, `expired`, `accepted` or
`cancelled`. Only a caller with the invited address gets it.

InvitationResponse.description:
A pending invitation: the invited address, its role, the catalog user id of the member who invited and their names as the catalog
holds them now, when it was created and expires, and its state at the moment of the request: `pending`, or `expired` once
its expiry has passed. It is never `accepted` or `cancelled`, because the list holds pending invitations
only, and inviting answers the new one.

InvitationResponseState.description:
The state of an invitation at the moment of the request: pending, expired (pending past its expiry), accepted (used) or cancelled
(revoked, replaced, or cancelled with its tenant). Every response that holds the state of an invitation uses this one enum, and says
which of its values it can hold.

InviteMemberRequest.description:
The address to invite, the built-in role the invitation gives, and the language of the invitation's email: without one, the
inviter's own. The role is required: a request without one is refused, so it never falls back to the enum's first value.

InviteOwnerRequest.description:
The address of the Owner the platform invites into a tenant without one, and the language of the invitation's email: without one, the
system admin's own.

InviterNameResponse.description:
Who invited: a user, with the names the catalog holds now and `deleted` for a user a system admin deleted, or the platform,
with no names and no `deleted`. The screen names the platform from `kind`, as the audit logs do.

InviterNameResponseKind.description: Who invited: a user of the tenant, or the platform, for which a system admin acted.

Language.description: A language the web speaks, by its BCP 47 language tag.

MemberResponse.description:
A member of the tenant: the user's id, the copy of their email address and name, their role, whether the identity provider deleted
the user, and when they joined the tenant. A deleted user has an empty email address and empty names, and
the screen shows "Deleted user", as the audit logs say `deleted` (K3).

MemberRole.description:
A built-in role: the built-in role of every role in a response, the role filter of the member and the invitation lists, the role an
invitation gives, and the role a member is given.

MeResponse.description:
The signed-in user: the catalog's id, not the identity provider's, the copy of their profile, whether they are a system admin, and
their preferences. It has no status: a suspended user is refused on every me endpoint (A9), and a deleted user cannot sign in.

MyTenantDetailResponse.description:
The tenant of the route, for one of its members: as an item of their tenant list, with when it was created and the names of the
permissions the member's role holds there, in ordinal order. The web shows an action only when the list holds its permission; every
endpoint still checks the permission itself.

MyTenantResponse.description:
A tenant the signed-in user belongs to: an item of their tenant list, and the tenant an invitation made them join. Its status is
active, or suspended or closed when its members cannot enter it. The role is the user's there.

MyTenantResponseStatus.description: The status of a tenant as its members see it: active, or suspended or closed when they cannot enter it.

OwnerInvitationResponse.description:
The latest Owner invitation of a tenant that has no Owner: its address, its expiry, and its state at the moment of the request:
`pending`, `expired` once its expiry has passed, or `cancelled`. It is never `accepted`, because it is shown only
while the tenant has no Owner.

Permission.description: A permission of the catalogue. Every endpoint checks its own permission.

PreferencesResponse.description: The user's preferences, which follow them to every tenant and device. A null time zone is not set.

errors.description: The field codes for each field of a request that failed validation, by the field's JSON name.

traceId.description: The trace id of the request, for the logs.

tenantIds.description: The tenants the error is about, when a client needs them to act, such as the tenants a user is the last Owner of.

RenameTenantRequest.description: A tenant's new name. The API trims it before it counts its length. The slug never changes.

RenameUserRequest.description: A user's new names, each within the API's limit. The API trims each name before it counts its length.

RoleResponse.description:
A role: the built-in role, or null for a custom role, which comes later (A3), and the role's stored name. A built-in role answers
`{ "builtIn": "owner", "name": "owner" }`. A client compares `builtIn` with MemberRole, never the name.

SuspendTenantRequest.description:
Why the system admin suspends the tenant, within the API's limit. The API trims the reason before it counts its length. A member
never sees it.

TenantDetailResponse.description: One tenant for the platform's detail screen: as an item of the list, with every Owner, in the order they joined, in place of the first.

TenantListItemResponse.description:
A tenant in the platform's list: as TenantResponse, with until when a closed tenant can be reopened, its members and Owners
counted, the Owner who joined first, and, while it has no Owner, its latest Owner invitation. Each is null when it does not apply.

TenantOwnerResponse.description: An Owner of a tenant: the catalog user's id, names and address.

TenantResponse.description:
A tenant and its status, with the reason of its suspension while it is suspended, or closed after a suspension, and the moment of its
closure while it is closed. Only a system admin sees this shape.

TenantResponseStatus.description: The status of a tenant: provisioning until its creation ends, then active, suspended or closed, or cancelled.

UserDetailResponse.description:
One catalog user for the user detail screen: as in the list, with when a system admin suspended them and that system admin's names
(null when the user is not suspended, or was suspended before step 20l), and every membership by the tenant's name.

UserMembershipResponse.description:
A tenant the user is a member of: its id, name, slug and status, the user's role there, when they joined, and whether they are
its last Owner. The suspend dialog warns with `lastOwner`, and the delete refusal names those tenants.

UserMembershipResponseTenantStatus.description: The status of a tenant a user is a member of: active, or suspended or closed when its members cannot enter it.

UserNameResponse.description:
A user's names as the catalog holds them now, resolved on read, as the audit names are (K3). A user a system admin deleted has no
names and `deleted`, and the screen shows "Deleted user". It holds no email address.

UserResponse.description:
A catalog user: the catalog's id, not the identity provider's, their email address and names, their status (active, suspended or
deleted), whether they are a system admin, how many tenants they are a member of, and when they joined the catalog.

UserResponseStatus.description: The status of a catalog user. A system admin deleted a deleted user, and the catalog keeps no email address or name of theirs.

bearer.description: A session token of the identity provider, in the Authorization header.
